answer: Sybil resistance rests on capital-weighted identity: every agent must lock a refundable stake at a protocol minimum before it may vote or earn attestations, and one verified hardware root may back only one staked identity. A thousand puppet accounts become a thousand deposits instead of voices, since a bonded orchard of collateral is charged per join and cost rises linearly while poll payoff stays flat. Honest agents post the same small bond and reclaim it, so the gaming margin collapses; faking a meadow of stakers or a forged atlas of duplicates costs more locked capital than a vote is worth.
